correctness.summary: The semidefinite common factor is uniquely P=(W1*W1)^(1/2), and every closure label Q satisfies W_N...W_1=Q P^N. Hence two labels differ by exactly a unitary fixing im(P) pointwise, giving the U(d-r) label fiber. Pairwise and multiple-intersection rank bounds follow from im(P) lying in the common equalizer of the labels, with the converse realized explicitly by (P,...,P,QP). The fixed-rank dimension formula follows from the complex Grassmannian dimension, positive Hermitian data on the support, and U(d-r) stabilizers. The N=2 specialization agrees with the source paper's explicit linear formula for C_Q.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Kotwal--Menon arXiv:2609.20159v1 prove only that every rank-deficient point of a closure belongs to at least one other closure; the inspected full text contains no exact all-label fiber, relative-unitary spectral intersection criterion, or fixed-rank multiple-intersection dimension formula. Synonymous searches did not locate that package. Singular polar-factor nonuniqueness itself is standard and is not claimed as new. Kotwal's 2026 Brown dissertation (DOI: 10.26300/bd6x-0503) was not inspected in full and remains the most plausible inaccessible source of related observations; the recent date of the motivating preprint adds residual risk.

value.summary: The result upgrades a qualitative overlap observation into a complete rank-stratified incidence law for the closure cover of the balanced variety. It identifies cover multiplicity as U(d-r), shows that pairwise overlap rank is exactly the 1-eigenspace multiplicity of the relative unitary, and gives explicit dimensions for every finite multiple-intersection rank stratum.

limitations: Only set-theoretic closure incidence and smooth fixed-rank strata are classified.
No special-Lagrangian integral-current extension across the singular locus is proved.
No local analytic normal forms, intersection multiplicities, or intersection angles are computed.
Kotwal's 2026 Brown dissertation (DOI: 10.26300/bd6x-0503) was not inspected in full.
The motivating preprint is recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
